gaps.title: Daily Outbound Messaging Rate Limiter
gaps.jtbd: When running outreach campaigns, I want to enforce strict daily message limits per Telegram account, so that our warmed-up accounts avoid getting spam-blocked or banned by Telegram flood control.
gaps.acceptanceCriteria: Given an active Telegram account and a campaign task, When messages are dispatched, Then the system must track outbound counts per account and halt dispatches once the daily limit (15-20 contacts per 24h) is reached.
gaps.reason: literal brief requirement: FEAT-ACC-05 explicitly specifies hard-coded strict limits on outbound conversations per account per day, which is entirely missing from the codebase.

gaps.title: Automatic Session Rotation and Failover
gaps.jtbd: When a Telegram account hits its daily dispatch limits or experiences flood errors, I want the system to dynamically switch campaign tasks to the next available account, so that campaigns continue without manual operator intervention.
gaps.acceptanceCriteria: Given a campaign running across a pool of connected Telegram accounts, When the active account encounters a FLOOD_WAIT error or reaches daily limits, Then the dynamic failover mechanism must automatically rotate the task to the next eligible account in the pool.
gaps.reason: literal brief requirement: FEAT-CMP-04 explicitly requests dynamic failover rotation to the next available account upon limit or error triggers, which is not implemented in the backend.

gaps.title: Frontend Integration with Onboarding, Campaigns, and Unified Inbox REST APIs
gaps.jtbd: When managing the platform, I want the Svelte UI to interact with backend REST controllers, so that operators can onboard accounts, import campaign lists, and read or reply to live conversation streams in real time.
gaps.acceptanceCriteria: Given the Svelte admin panel, When an operator uploads a CSV list, onboards an account, or sends/receives a message, Then the frontend must communicate with the corresponding backend controllers and persist the changes instead of utilizing static mock data.
gaps.reason: literal brief requirement: FEAT-ACC-01, FEAT-CMP-01, and FEAT-CRM-01 require functional UI capabilities for OTP/session onboarding, lead CSV list ingestion, and a unified chat inbox. The Svelte frontend contains only static mock data and has no integration with the backend REST APIs.

gaps.title: Admin Dashboard Authentication and Authorization
gaps.jtbd: When accessing the self-hosted admin panel, I want to authenticate via secure credentials, so that unauthorized users are prevented from accessing or manipulating sensitive Telegram accounts, session data, and proxies.
gaps.acceptanceCriteria: Given an unauthorized user accessing the admin panel URL, When they attempt to view dashboard pages or invoke API controllers, Then the system must block access and redirect them to a secure login page, requiring correct admin credentials to proceed.
gaps.reason: domain-standard expectation: Any private self-hosted SaaS-style admin panel handling sensitive credentials (like Telegram session files and proxies) implicitly requires secure authentication and user session management.

gaps.title: Telegram Outbound Message Queue and Retry Resilience Mechanism
gaps.jtbd: When sending outbound campaign messages under unstable network or API conditions, I want the system to route dispatches through a message queue with automatic retries, so that no messages are lost due to transient bridge disconnects.
gaps.acceptanceCriteria: Given an outbound message dispatch request, When the JNI/JNA bridge experiences a transient connection timeout or failure, Then the system must queue the message for automatic retry and update its delivery status instead of silently failing or dropping the message.
gaps.reason: domain-standard expectation: A real-time Telegram outreach platform with high network dependency requires a robust queuing and retry/resilience mechanism for outbound message delivery.
